name: Coupling components of components yields an isomorphic resultant
description: Exercise 4.86: if Z@ = RSY(SCR), VSCR = (Z1,...,Zn), each Zi = RSY(SCRi) with VSCRi = (Zi1,...,Zimi), VSCR$ = (Z11,...,Z1m1,...,Zn1,...,Znmn) is a connectable vector and CSCR$ = {(OP@(SCRi, Zi)(OhZi), IP@(SCRk, Zk)(IjZk)) : (OhZi, IjZk) in CSCR} union {CSCRi : i in IJS[1, n]}, then Z@ = ISY(Z@$, HS, HI, HO) where Z@$ = RSY(SCR$), HS maps (x11,...,xnmn) to ((x11,...,x1m1),...,(xn1,...,xnmn)), HI = ID(IZ@$) and HO = ID(OZ@$).

elements.text: For each i in IJS[1, n], Zi = RSY(SCRi) with VSCRi = (Zi1,...,Zimi) for mi in IJS+; VSCR and VSCR$ are connectable vectors.
CSCR$ = {(OP@(SCRi, Zi)(OhZi), IP@(SCRk, Zk)(IjZk)) : (OhZi, IjZk) in CSCR} union {CSCRi : i in IJS[1, n]}.
IZ@$ = IZ@: an input port of VSCR$ is unconnected in SCR$ exactly when it is unconnected in its own SCRi and the corresponding external port of Zi is unconnected in SCR.
OZ@$ = OZ@: an output port of VSCR$ is unconnected in SCR$ exactly when it is unconnected in its own SCRi and the corresponding external port of Zi is unconnected in SCR.
Resolving a component input through CSCR$ in one step agrees with resolving it in two steps: the external input of Zi = RSY(SCRi) through CSCR, then the component input inside SCRi.
Z@$ = ISY(Z@, HS, HI, HO): HS, HI and HO are bijections that preserve next state and readout.
Z@ = ISY(Z@$, HS, HI, HO) where Z@$ = RSY(SCR$).
